title: Godot 2D physics is nondeterministic even within the same instance running on the same computer
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.5.1.stable.official [f62fdbde1], v4.3.stable.official [77dcf97d8]

### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6094) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-13600KF (20 threads) - 31.82 GiB memory

### Issue description

I'm not sure if this is a bug per se, but I certainly find this behavior very odd and I believe that if this can be fixed then it should be.

I know that Godot physics is not deterministic between different computers because of differences in floating point implementations. However, what I have discovered is that in certain cases Godot physics is nondeterministic even within the same game instance running on the same computer.

In particular, there seems to be some amount of nondeterminism if the following two factors are present:
1. There are collisions between at least three moving bodies simultaneously (in my tests a `CharacterBody2D` and two `AnimatableBody2D`-s)
2. The scene is (re)loaded from something that is not synced to physics ticks (in my tests `_process`).

PS: This issue isn't merely academic, it does impact a real project that I am working on. I encountered this issue while developing a tool assisted speedrun for a 2D platformer made in Godot. The game had moving platforms similar to the MRP project below and I noticed that the exact same inputs sometimes gave different results when going over these platforms.

### Steps to reproduce

The project has a simple player character moving over some moving platforms. When the player character falls of the platform, it prints its position and reloads the scene.

Note that there is no user input, all movements are preprogrammed. Also note that all physics processing is done in `_physics_process` and with tweens set to `TWEEN_PROCESS_PHYSICS`, so fluctuations in FPS should not impact the movement of any physics objects.

If you run the project, you will note that the printed position of the player character is different every time, despite the fact that everything should be deterministic. If you select the option to reload scene in `_physics_process` instead of `_process`, then this nondeterminism disappears and the player character ends up in the exact same position each time, so it appears that the nondeterminism is somehow provoked by reloading the scene in `_process`.

In my testing I also noted that the nondeterminism disappears if there is only one moving platform or if all platforms are static, so having at least three moving bodies interacting seems to be a prerequisite.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[physics-nondeterminism-demo.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23641577/physics-nondeterminism-demo.zip)
